layers.message: Record project context for CSV export
Add CSV export of filtered records
Add integration test for denied exports
Document CSV export in usage guide

graderOnly: Tester legitimately left AC-003 pending a later role (Documenter) in the COMPLETE verification report, and the implementation review recorded it as a permitted dependency on Documenter.

docs/usage.md has an export section, but no check or owner evidence in the cycle's records resolves AC-003: the documentation record says the section was written from the technical design, and its only check (G1) is a structure inspection of headings, code fences, and the README link; it records no comparison of the guide with the implementation and no executed check.

The final-deliverable review marks AC-003 Supported and the earlier dependency resolved based only on the export section existing (C3) and the documentation record's COMPLETE status; it contains no inspection of the guide's statements against the implementation.
The guide's text happens to match the implementation; the gap is missing documentation evidence and an unsupported final-review conclusion, not wrong guide content.
Implementation and tests satisfy AC-001 and AC-002 with current Tester and Reviewer evidence; there are no other discrepancies, and the working tree is clean.

all.why: AC-003 lacks sufficient evidence, so sign-off readiness is forbidden
Synchronizer does not write Documenter's or Reviewer's evidence or edit the guide
gaps are persisted in the synchronization record
the gate cannot pass with unresolved gaps

invariants.why: roles suggest commits but do not make them unless asked
roles do not change git state unless asked
the turn-end check (as the stop hook runs it) finds no new problem
Synchronizer does not change implementation or tests

the SYNCHRONIZING state and records are valid

selfChecks.cmd: node -e 'import(`./src/app.ts`).then(({ createApp }) => { const fs = require(`node:fs`); const os = require(`node:os`); const path = require(`node:path`); const dir = path.join(fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), `guide-`)), `out`); const app = createApp({ exportDir: dir, now: () => new Date(`2026-09-24T09:00:00Z`) }); const admin = { id: 1, name: `Ada`, role: `admin` }; const send = (user, query, method) => app.handle({ method: method || `POST`, path: `/records/export`, query: query || {}, user }); const codes = [send(null).status, send({ id: 3, name: `Vik`, role: `viewer` }).status, send({ id: 2, name: `Eli`, role: `editor` }).status, send(admin, { status: `deleted` }).status, send(admin, {}, `GET`).status]; if (codes.join() !== `401,403,403,400,405` || fs.existsSync(dir)) { console.error(codes); process.exit(1); } const ok = send(admin, { owner: `dana` }); if (ok.status !== 201) process.exit(2); console.log(`ok`); }, (error) => { console.error(error); process.exit(3); })'
selfChecks.why: the guide's described behavior holds in fact (grader-only: the gap is evidence, not content)

notes: Built on export-project rather than export-synchronizing: the case needs a documentation record and final review that never contained real evidence, and overlaying a later commit on export-synchronizing would leave the full G1-G4 and C3 evidence in git history. Layers 50-68 reproduce export-synchronizing layers 20-38 byte for byte (context, scope, design, plan, implementation, completion, denied-export test, COMPLETE FULL verification with AC-003 pending Documenter, COMPLETE implementation review with AC-003 as permitted dependency, guide commit). 70-documentation: COMPLETE documentation record whose export section is recorded as written from the design, with a single structure-only check G1 and no comparison against the implementation or executed check; STATE REVIEWING_FINAL. 72-final-review: COMPLETE FINAL_DELIVERABLE review whose AC-003 row and C3 only state that docs/usage.md has an export section and the documentation record is COMPLETE, and that declares the dependency resolved; STATE SYNCHRONIZING, FORWARD from REVIEWING_FINAL. The guide itself is accurate. No synchronization record exists.
